name: Banking system stress
summary: Financial stress gauges low: St Louis Fed index -0.49 and ECB stress indicator 0.0065; no notable bank failure found
state: The St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index was -0.49 in the week to 6 Nov and the ECB's systemic stress indicator was 0.0065 on 12 Nov, with a 20-day high of only 0.025, far below the Watch lines (FRED; ECB). No mid-sized or larger US or European bank failure or rescue was found as of 14 Nov.
for_you: Banking conditions are calm. UK deposits are protected up to the FSCS limit; the FSCS website explains the cover.
rubric_hit: STLFSI -0.49 < 0 and ECB CISS 0.0065 < 0.25, no notable bank failure = Normal

sources.title: FRED — St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index (STLFSI4)
ECB Data Portal — Composite Indicator of Systemic Stress

why: Bank failures turn market losses into credit crunches; 2008 and 2023 both began as 'contained' bank problems.
drivers: Rate shocks to bond portfolios, commercial property losses, deposit flight, private-credit links.

rubric.alert: STLFSI > 1.5, or ECB CISS > 0.45, or a systemically important bank fails or needs rescue, or emergency central-bank facilities launched.
rubric.watch: STLFSI 0–1.5, or ECB CISS 0.25–0.45, or a mid-sized bank failure/rescue, or a large bank under visible funding pressure.
rubric.normal: St Louis Fed Financial Stress Index < 0, ECB CISS < 0.25, and no notable bank failures or rescues.
